stories.title: Nepal: Hundreds reported missing after deadly flash floods
stories.summary: Entire roads and villages have been engulfed in mud after flash floods struck a border crossing between Tibet and Nepal. Hundreds are reported missing, including over 300 tourists. Flood alerts have also been issued in the Indian states of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.
stories.headline: Nepal: Hundreds reported missing after deadly flash floods

opening: Entire roads and villages have been engulfed in mud after flash floods struck a border crossing between Tibet and Nepal.
Hundreds are reported missing, including over 300 tourists.
body: Flood alerts have also been issued in the Indian states of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.
Across the border, Tibet reported ‘major casualties’ with people missing in the neighbouring county of Gyirong.
At least 95 people have been killed and hundreds are missing after a huge flash flood swept away villages in Nepal, damaging roads, bridges and power projects in areas near Tibet, authorities said.

Officials in Nepal said at least 384 tourists, including 291 from countries including the United Kingdom, the United States, India and Malaysia were reported missing as a result of the flash flood on Wednesday.
“So far 95 deaths have been reported,” police spokesman Abi Narayan Kafle said, adding that 28 police personnel were also missing.

Narendra Pariyar urged those living on the banks of the Bhote Koshi River in the area to seek higher ground, pointing to reports that nearby villages and infrastructure project sites were washed away.
“We have asked both India and China to help us with the rescue efforts,” said Sasmit Pokharel, a Nepali government spokesperson.

Across the border, Tibet reported “major casualties” with people missing in the neighbouring county of Gyirong after a mudslide hit a land crossing between China and Nepal, the Xinhua official news agency said.
The mudslide hit China’s Gyirong port, cutting off roads, communications and power in the Shigatse region, Xinhua added, without giving details.
President Xi Jinping urged “all-out” efforts to search for the missing, and called for strengthening monitoring and early warning systems to prevent secondary disasters.
Prayash Adhikari, a climate justice activist in Nepal, said the “devastating” flood has wiped out “whole villages”.
“Hundreds of people are missing,” Adhikari told Al Jazeera from Kathmandu, stating it wiped out buildings, schools, bridges and highways.

bullets.label: Next
bullets.text: The waters were too high for helicopters to land in Nepal’s affected areas of Syapru Besi and Timure in the mountainous district of Rasuwa, with a population of about 50,000, officials said.

stories.title: UK minister condemns 'outrageous' Israeli seizure of Unrwa training centre
stories.summary: UK minister condemns 'outrageous' Israeli seizure of Unrwa training centre Stephen Doughty, British minister of state for the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan, has issued a statement condemning the Israeli seizure of Unrwa's Qalandiya Training Centre in occupied East Jerusalem as "outrageous". “This UN facility has offered generations of Palestinian refugees education & opportunity,” Doughty said in a post on X. The minister urged that “Israel must comply with its obligations and respect inviolability of UN premises.” Israeli forces stormed and occupied the Unrwa centre on Tuesday, and continue their occupation of the building.
